name: Shai-Hulud npm Supply-Chain Worm
description: Shai-Hulud is a self-propagating npm supply-chain worm that compromises maintainer accounts and CI/CD tokens to publish trojanized package versions, which themselves harvest further credentials and re-propagate. A 'Mini Shai-Hulud' variant disclosed in April 2026 targets SAP npm packages via malicious preinstall scripts that execute before most security tooling runs. On May 11, 2026, Microsoft identified a major resurgence compromising 170+ npm packages and 2 PyPI packages across 404 malicious versions, followed by a burst of 300+ malicious versions across 323 packages published in just 22 minutes on May 19. New variants persist via AI coding agent configuration files (Claude Code, VS Code), turning developer tooling into a propagation vector. TeamPCP has publicly claimed authorship of the Mini Shai-Hulud branding, and the related Miasma cluster's June 2026 wave reuses overlapping techniques against npm and PyPI.

mitre_techniques.technique_name: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
mitre_techniques.notes: Trojanized npm/PyPI package versions published via compromised maintainer accounts
Harvests npm publish tokens, CI/CD secrets, and cloud credentials from developer environments
Malicious preinstall/postinstall scripts execute automatically during npm install
Stolen maintainer credentials used to publish additional malicious package versions, enabling self-propagation
Persistence via tampered AI coding agent configuration files (Claude Code, VS Code) on developer workstations

notable_examples: April 29, 2026: Aikido researchers disclosed 'Mini Shai-Hulud' targeting SAP npm packages via malicious preinstall scripts
May 11, 2026: Microsoft identified a resurgence compromising 170+ npm packages and 2 PyPI packages across 404 malicious versions
May 19, 2026: 300+ malicious package versions across 323 packages published in a 22-minute automated burst
June 1-2, 2026: Miasma cluster's wave hit 50+ additional npm packages plus a related 'Hades' PyPI wave (37 wheels across 19 packages)
TeamPCP publicly claimed authorship of the Mini Shai-Hulud branding and tooling
detection_opportunities: Monitor npm/PyPI install logs for anomalous preinstall/postinstall script execution
Alert on outbound network connections originating from package install processes
Audit CI/CD pipeline tokens and AI coding agent (Claude Code, VS Code, Copilot) config files for unexpected modification or credential exposure
Pin dependency versions and review diffs on transitive dependency updates before allowing them into builds
Cross-reference installed package versions against published IOC lists from Aikido, Akamai, Snyk, and Microsoft
Require short-lived, scoped npm publish tokens with mandatory 2FA for maintainer accounts
